next_event.source: doc 112075, Shafer 2026-07-30: 'We expect to share our conclusion on that assessment [China] by our next quarterly earnings call' (Q3 2026 call, date not stated). No Investor Day announced; last Investor Day 2023-11-06 (doc 85150).

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Dated margin target exists only at segment level: North America water treatment (about $250M of sales) operating margin up 200 bps to about 15% in 2026 and about 200 bps more in 2027. Company-level framing is a one-year 2026 guide of about 24% North America segment margin and 6%-7% Rest of World, flat to down versus 2025. No consolidated EBITDA margin target. SCORING NOTE: C scored 2, not 3: a literal reading of the rubric gives 3 for the CEO's dated water treatment margin level (15% in 2026) and $6M-$8M 2027 savings, but both apply to a segment of about 6% of sales and are worth under 1% of EBITDA. The company-level framing is a one-year segment margin guide (a 2). Literal scoring would make the total 10. B scored 3 because Shafer was hired from outside (3M) and the CFO is external, with a Chairman change and an acquisition in window; a stricter reading of Shafer as an internal promotion gives B = 2. A 'water treatment operating margin improvement' guide also appears in data_guidance dated 2026-01-29 (Q4 2025 call), not fetched.

street.gap_assumption: The only dated target is a segment operating margin (water treatment, about 6% of sales) and cannot be compared with consolidated EBITDA consensus, so no gap is computed. Calendar fiscal year, Baba FY labels equal company years. Sizing: +200 bps on about $250M of sales is about $5M, or 0.6% of FY2026 consensus EBITDA; the $6M-$8M savings midpoint is under 1%.

evidence_of_progress.note: VA EBITDA margin yoy for Q4 2025 (+117 bps) and Q1 2026 (-147 bps). VA has not yet loaded Q2 2026 actuals; per Lauber (doc 112075) Q2 2026 North America adjusted segment margin was 24.4%, down 100 bps, and China sales fell 28% in local currency. LTM uses Q2 2025 to Q1 2026. Steel costs guided about 15% higher in 2026; price increases of 4%-7% announced.

verdict: Full leadership reset (outside-hired CEO, external CFO, new Chairman) plus a pending China decision on a stabilized, 1st-percentile multiple, but no company-level margin target yet.
open_questions: Does the China assessment (due by the Q3 2026 call) end in an exit or partnership, and what does that do to consolidated margin given Rest of World runs 6%-7% versus about 24% in North America?
Will Shafer and Anderson put a consolidated margin or EBITDA target with a year on the table, for example at a new Investor Day?
How much of the 2026 margin pressure is steel and tariff timing that the 4%-7% price increases recover?
